summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant abdominal pain, similar to prior flares. She presented with severe pain and nausea unresponsive to home medications, including gabapentin, tramadol, and diazepam suppositories. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal or pelvic pathology, and labs were stable. She was admitted for pain control and started on indomethacin, with recommendations from the pain team to increase gabapentin and tizanidine doses. Her bipolar disorder remained stable on lithium, and asthma and GERD were managed with home medications. She improved with treatment, was discharged home after two days, and advised to follow up with her pain clinic and OB/GYN, continue indomethacin for two weeks with kidney function monitoring, and receive her scheduled Lupron injection.
